ARC-4.note: The architecture, ownership, format and coverage checks run only against the job's module in its gate, layer checks when a layer closes, and over the whole product before a release or when I ask for one.

ENF-1.note: at most a handful of command hooks, each for a zero-exception rule, each with a legitimate blocked exit; none that hold a turn or judge text.

ENF-6.note: native /goal with a mechanical condition (PR state on GitHub), no model judging the transcript. Superseded by Bob's word, walk-through question 2, 1 Nov ("Yes, as recommended"): no /goal, since its check is a model reading the conversation; a stopped job is caught by status and the sweep. Recorded by the coordinator, 3 Nov, walk-through question 36.

GAP-1.note: A tranche CAN RUN from open to close with no one watching: every stop is a named blocker in the record, BOB starts other work meanwhile, and only a blocker that only Bob can clear reaches him.

INT-4.note: Bob's word, walk-through question 3, 1 Nov ("Yes, as recommended"), with his ARC-4 note: a layer closes when every PR is merged and the layer's checks pass; whole-product checks run before a release or when Bob asks; the next layer starts at once. Recorded by the coordinator, 3 Nov, walk-through question 36.

JOB-13.note: Suggest: later, after the first tranche, on payment and data paths only.

JOB-14.note: As suggested (keep) but the restarted session should recognize that corrections were made and try to understand why to anticipate all other needed corrections so it doesn't continue to fail.

JOB-7.note: Suggest: Evidence is a machine-readable receipt (command, exit code, git SHA, and an explicit not-verified list), never prose.

MNT-1.note: Suggest: yes, but as the thin process this ledger describes, not as the twelve-module architecture of MNT-2.

MNT-8.note: Certification is a long-term goal that indicates that it's ready for general use. Suggest: one shadow of a representative slice, then the live first tranche is the certification with SES-11 and SES-12 measured; a full 128-module shadow per release is itself a token sink.

P1.note: Keep as Process3's purpose, with my 3 Nov words added: quickly and cheaply, behaviour that survives, my time only where it is mine.

P10.note: Keep concurrency, which was lost and is why Phase 2 planned only two jobs, and keep nothing waits. Drop jobs stay active until all are complete: under Process3 a job ends at its merge (INT-1, INT-4) and a later service change reaches its users by GAT-3.

P13.note: Keep the cost reason and the rule; the threshold stays in the start table (SES-4, SES-6) rather than a fixed 40%.

P17.note: Keep it whole after onboarding; no Ledger line holds it today. Your word, 3 Nov: during onboarding the platform forces a few GitHub steps of yours; keep those as few as possible, each walked through.

P19.note: Keep. PLN-2 holds the plan rule and SES-17 a nudge, but BOB never idles and never stops for Bob were lost. Drop overcome by code where it would mean a hook: the mechanism is the tool naming the next act and the sweep's wake, never anything that holds a turn (ENF-1, ENF-3), and it must be shown efficient and effective (my word, 3 Nov).

P2.note: The build state is what tells BOB what to do. Process3 keeps requirements and layers at the product's own paths, so one subtree becomes the paths the product's config names.

P20.note: Keep the evidence rule, which the Ledger lost. Process3 already decided that no hook refuses a short read (ENF-4 dropped) and that reads are a matter of record (REC-8).

P21.note: Keep for questions that are Bob's by P17 only. Lanes stay as SES-14 (modify) and SES-15 settled them.

P3.note: Development under Process3 is development of that product, not of Process3. A serious enough flaw pauses the product, Process3 is fixed separately, and the product resumes on the fixed version. Changes during Process3's own first build are expected.

P7.note: Keep no requirement goes untested, which was lost (JOB-12 only checks that tests are not inert). Keep the mechanical pass, shorter: it is the efficient route for changes that need no judgment.

PLT-2.note: Bob's word in chat, 3 Nov (written here by the coordinator): depend only on acts the committed approvals cover and that were measured to pass; archiving sessions and switching off or deleting tasks are housekeeping, counted and reported, never needed for correctness.

PLT-5.note: Bob's word in chat, 3 Nov, option A (written here by the coordinator): no session starts its own successor; depth stays at most 3 (coordinator, ROOT, BOB, job), as ran on 3 Nov when the explore and review jobs merged at depth 3. The watcher is started beside ROOT by whoever starts ROOT.

REC-1.note: keep the split, but move coordination traffic to PR bodies, comments and issues, or to a separate bookkeeping repository; add the size check in REC-10.

REC-8.note: keep the audit, but judge reading by what a session can cite from the end of a document, and shrink documents so the question rarely arises.

REC-9.note: Try this, but measure the experience with an open mind as to whether it's work or not.

REQ-6.note: Suggest: a cap that triggers a split or consolidation by BOB before any job starts, measured on the real product; never a refusal at a job's start.

SES-1.note: Suggest: ROOT's creation of sessions moves to a scheduled task that creates a fresh session on each firing where possible; ROOT as a session only where a message must be answered.

SES-14.note: Suggest: a lane is a knowledge directory and design responsibility plus an on-demand worker BOB starts with that directory as its reading set; a long-lived lane only where measured worthwhile. The lifecycle of a lane includes refreshes that BOB manages to keep the session depth consistant.

SES-15.note: Bob's word, settled 1 Nov (Foundations, open tension 4): BOB routes every request between spokes and translates only where a requester cannot use the answer as given; toward Bob it always explains each decision of his with context, options and a recommendation. Routing share measured after the first layer. Recorded by the coordinator, 3 Nov, walk-through question 36.

SES-16.note: Suggest: I'm skeptical, but let's measure on the first tranche, comparing tokens per wake against the handoff cost already paid.

SES-8.note: Models, effort, and permissions mode come from one table, picked by the start command; always a model and effort sufficient for quality, and a permissions mode appropriate for the task at hand.

TXT-1.note: Bob's word, walk-through question 7, 1 Nov ("Yes, as recommended"): hand-written means BOB writes and keeps the product's CLAUDE.md line by line, each line passing the per-line test, never by /init or a tool reading the repository, with no approval needed and each change listed in the tranche report; the approvals block stays Bob's own. Recorded by the coordinator, 3 Nov, walk-through question 36.

TXT-4.note: Suggest: I'm skeptical, but let's try to apply TXT-2 to the principles too; most roles need two or three of them.
